Code must compile with `rustc` or as a Cargo project. 2. **CLI arguments**: The Rust binary must accept exactly the same command-line arguments as the C++ binary (same names, defaults, and required fields). Parse args via `std::env::args()`. 3. **Logic and output**: Algorithm logic, numeric precision, and string formatting must exactly match the C++ source. `println!` output must be byte-for-byte identical to `std::cout` output. 4. **Zero external dependencies**: Do NOT use any crates from crates.io (only `std`). Forbidden crates for this repo: none. Implement all functionality from scratch using the standard library. 5. **Project structure**: Create a complete Cargo project in `/output`. Organize library code into modules. Place the entry test file `test15.rs` in the package root `/output`. 6. **Black-box implementation**: Do not read the C++ library source. Infer behavior from the interface, then re-implement using `std`. 7. **Output**: - Create and implement library files inside `/output`. - Save the entry file to `/output/test15.rs`. - Compile and produce an executable at `/output/test15.rs` (by running `rustc test15.rs` or `cargo build --release`). Hint: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable` is the compiled C++ binary — use it to debug with any arguments.

Investigation complete. Here is the full behavioral specification.

## Program structure (`test15_executable`)

- `initialize()` produces no observable output. With no arguments: no output, exit 0.
- For `i = 1 .. min(argc-1, 5)` (i.e. only `argv[1]`–`argv[5]`; extra args ignored), prints one line each:
  1. `pluralize(argv[i])`
  2. `camelize(argv[i])`
  3. `underscore(argv[i])` — only when `i` is even (i=2, 4)
- Then, if `argc > 1`, prints three more lines: `isPlural(argv[1])` (`0`/`1`), `isSingular(argv[1])`, `demodulize("Module::" + argv[1])`.
- Every line is `\n`-terminated (including a trailing empty line when a result is empty). No prompts, no extra whitespace.
- If `demodulize` throws (see below), all prior stdout lines are printed, then libstdc++ terminate message on stderr: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range' / what(): basic_string::substr: __pos (which is N) > this->size() (which is M)`, process dies with SIGABRT, exit code **134**.

## `pluralize(w)` — naive

- `""` → `""`
- If `w` exactly (case-sensitive) equals one of the 10 uncountables `equipment, information, rice, money, species, series, fish, sheep, jeans, police` → `w` unchanged.
- Otherwise → `w + "s"`. No other rules whatsoever: `box→boxs`, `bus→buss`, `church→churchs`, `category→categorys`, `person→persons`, `child→childs`, `mouse→mouses`, `knife→knifes`, `news→newss` (news is NOT uncountable), `Fish→Fishs`, `Jeans→Jeanss`, `" fish"→" fishs"`, `"fish "→"fish s"`, `salmon→salmons`, `_`→`_s`, non-ASCII untouched (`café→cafés`... byte append).

## `camelize(w)` — lower camelCase, underscores only

Byte-wise state machine: skip every `_` byte; the first non-underscore byte after any run of underscores is passed through single-byte `toupper` (C locale; non-ASCII bytes unchanged). Nothing else is changed — the first character is NOT uppercased, and `-`/space/digits are untouched.

- `hello_world→helloWorld`, `active_record→activeRecord`, `dog→dog`, `HelloWorld→HelloWorld`, `HELLO_WORLD→HELLOWORLD`, `x_y_z→xYZ`
- `_hello→Hello`, `_a_b→AB`, `a__b→aB`, `a_→a`, `_→""`, `__→""`, `""→""`
- `hello-world→hello-world`, `a_1→a1`, `héllo_wörld→hélloWörld`, `a_é→aé` (byte `0xC3` unchanged)

## `underscore(w)` — naive camelCase→snake

Byte-wise over original index `i`: if byte is ASCII `A–Z`, append `_` iff `i > 0`, then append the lowercased byte; else append byte unchanged.

- `HelloWorld→hello_world`, `activeRecord→active_record`, `A→a`, `AB→a_b`, `aB→a_b`, `a1B→a1_b`
- NO acronym collapsing: `HELLOWORLD→h_e_l_l_o_w_o_r_d`, `HTMLParser→h_t_m_l_parser`, `ABCDef→a_b_c_def`, `XMLHttpRequest→x_m_l_http_request`
- Existing `_` kept verbatim (can double up): `Foo_Bar→foo__bar`, `_A→__a`, `snake_case_already→snake_case_already`, `ÉmileTest→Émile_test` (non-ASCII bytes untouched), `""→""`

## `demodulize(s)` — buggy substring

Exactly `s.substr(s.rfind(':') + 2)` — note **single-char** `rfind(':')` and `+2`, so it drops the last colon **plus one extra byte**:
- Called here as `demodulize("Module::" + argv[1])`; since the prefix always contains `::`, `rfind` never fails in-program.
- `dog` → `"og"`, `person` → `"erson"`, `a` → `""`, `ab` → `"b"` (i.e. `argv[1].substr(1)` when `argv[1]` has no `:`)
- `X::Y` → `""`, `X::YY` → `"Y"`, `ns::deep::Name` → `"ame"`, `a:b:c` → `""`, `x:y` → `""`
- **Crash (uncaught `std::out_of_range`, SIGABRT, rc 134)** iff the last `:` is the final byte, i.e. `argv[1]` is empty or ends with `:` (`""`, `:`, `::`, `x:` all abort — after the normal preceding output).
- (Out of program reach: with no `:` in `s`, `npos+2` wraps to `1` → `substr(1)`.)

## `isPlural(w)` / `isSingular(w)`

`isSingular(w)` is always exactly `!isPlural(w)` (verified on ~200 probes; printed as `0`/`1`). Everything is **case-sensitive and byte-oriented**. `isPlural(w)` behaves as "a Rails-2.x-style `singularize(w)` would change `w`", which reduces to:

`isPlural(w) = false` if `w` is in the uncountable list (same 10 words, exact lowercase), or `w` matches `/(n)ews$/` (`news`, `xnews` → 0; but `newss` → 1), or `w == "analysis"`, or `w == "crisis"`.

Otherwise `isPlural(w) = true` iff any of:
- `w` ends in lowercase `s` (generic rule: `cats`, `buses`, `classes`, `wishes`, `quizzes`, `matrices`, `vertices`, `indices`, `toes`, `shoes`, `heroes`, `potatoes`, `analyses`, `bases`, `theses`, `syntheses`, `wives`, `knives`, `wolves`, `thieves`, `movies`, `categories`, `babies`, `soliloquies`, `tives`, `hives`, `statuses`, `aliases`, `crises`, `testes`, `gas`, `this`, `is`, `s`, `ss`, `ies`, `bus`, `class`, `status`, `cactus`, `focus`, `thesis`, `basis`, `diagnosis`, `axis`, `alias` → all 1)
- `w` matches `/(octop|vir)i$/` (`octopi`, `viri` → 1; `cacti`, `foci`, `OCTOPI` → 0)
- `w` matches `/^(m|l)ice$/` (`mice`, `lice` → 1; `dice`, `Mice` → 0)
- `w` matches `/([ti])a$/` (`data`, `media`, `criteria`, `ta`, `ia` → 1; `na`, `phenomena`, `DATA` → 0)

Otherwise `false` (`dog`, `box`, `quiz`, `church`, `hero`, `potato`, `child`, `man`, `men`, `women`, `children`, `feet`, `teeth`, `geese`, `people`, `ox`, `oxen`→1 via... no: `oxen`→1 because... `oxen` ends in `n`? — observed `oxen`→**1**; recheck: `oxen` printed `1`. It doesn't fit the compact rules above! Hmm.)

Wait — `oxen` → `1` was observed. It ends in `n`, no rule above matches. That breaks the compact form: there must be an `/^(ox)en$/ → ox` singular rule. So add: `w` matches `/^oxen$/` (anchored; starts with `oxen`: Rails rule is `/^(ox)en/i`) → 1. Similarly recheck other non-s matches observed: `mice`/`lice` (rule), `octopi`/`viri` (rule), `data`/`media`/`criteria` (rule), `oxen` (rule). All other 1-results end in `s`. So the complete extra patterns are: `/^(ox)en/`, `/(octop|vir)i$/`, `/^(m|l)ice$/`, `/([ti])a$/`.

Also noteworthy case results: `CATS→0`, `BUS→0`, `NEWS→0`, `News→1`, `Analysis→1`, `CRISIS→0`, `Series→1`, `Fish→0`, `xcrisis→1`, `xanalysis→1`, `xnews→0` — confirming lowercase, case-sensitive patterns with `^`-anchored `analysis`/`crisis`/`mice`/`lice`/`oxen` rules and unanchored `(n)ews$`, `(octop|vir)i$`, `([ti])a$`.

## Representative observations

```
$ test15_executable dog          → dogs / dog / 0 / 1 / og
$ test15_executable dog cat      → dogs dog cats cat cat 0 1 og   (underscore(cat) at i=2)
$ test15_executable a b c d e f g→ as a bs b b cs c ds d d es e 0 1 «»   (f,g ignored)
$ test15_executable hello_world  → hello_worlds / helloWorld / 0 / 1 / ello_world
$ test15_executable x HTMLParser → xs x HTMLParser HTMLParsers h_t_m_l_parser 0 1 x
$ test15_executable ""           → «» «» 0 1 then std::out_of_range abort (rc 134)
$ test15_executable "X::YY"      → X::YYs / X::YY / 0 / 1 / Y
$ test15_executable news         → newss / news / 0 / 1 / ews
$ test15_executable mice         → mices / mice / 1 / 0 / ice
```

Caveat: `isPlural`'s compact form is inferred from ~200 black-box probes; the underlying implementation is likely a full Rails-2.x-style singular-rule list, but every rule that changes a word (except the four non-`s` patterns listed) is behaviorally subsumed by "ends in lowercase `s`" for a boolean check, and all self-mapping exceptions found are `news`, `analysis`, `crisis`, plus the uncountables.

# Plan: Rust migration of `test15.cpp`

## Behavioral baseline

Black-box probing of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable` established:

- Process only `argv[1]` through `argv[5]`; ignore extras.
- For each retained argument, print `pluralize(arg)` and `camelize(arg)`; for argument positions 2 and 4 also print `underscore(arg)`.
- If at least one argument exists, print `isPlural(argv[1])`, `isSingular(argv[1])`, and `demodulize("Module::" + argv[1])`, one result per line.
- `pluralize` appends ASCII `s` except for the exact lowercase uncountables: `equipment`, `information`, `rice`, `money`, `species`, `series`, `fish`, `sheep`, `jeans`, `police`.
- `camelize` is lower-camel case over underscores: remove `_`, ASCII-uppercase the byte following each underscore run, and leave the initial byte and all non-underscore separators unchanged.
- `underscore` ASCII-lowercases every uppercase byte and inserts `_` before it when its original byte index is greater than zero; it does not collapse acronyms or existing underscores.
- `demodulize` behaves like the C++ substring after `rfind(':') + 2`, including its unusual off-by-one behavior. In this program the `Module::` prefix guarantees a colon. If the computed position is beyond the string (empty argument or argument ending in `:`), terminate with abort after the preceding lines.
- `isSingular` is the boolean negation of `isPlural`.
- `isPlural` is case-sensitive. It is false for the uncountable list, strings ending in `news`, and exactly `analysis` or `crisis`; otherwise true for strings ending in lowercase `s`, ending in `octopi`/`viri`, exactly `mice`/`lice`/`oxen`, or ending in `ta`/`ia`.

## Implementation steps

1. Create `/output/Cargo.toml` for a Rust 2021 package with no dependencies and an explicit binary target:
   - package/library source under `/output/src/`
   - binary entry at `/output/test15.rs` via `[[bin]] name = "test15", path = "test15.rs"`
2. Create `/output/src/lib.rs` exporting an `inflection` module.
3. Create `/output/src/inflection.rs` with byte-oriented functions matching C locale/C++ byte behavior:
   - `pluralize(&str) -> String`
   - `camelize(&str) -> String`
   - `underscore(&str) -> String`
   - `is_plural(&str) -> bool`
   - `is_singular(&str) -> bool`
   - `demodulize(&str) -> String`
   Keep transformations ASCII-only so Unicode UTF-8 bytes are preserved instead of using Rust Unicode case conversion.
4. Implement `/output/test15.rs` with `std::env::args()`, reproduce the C++ argument-count loop and line order, print booleans as `0`/`1`, and mirror the `demodulize` failure path by aborting after prior output when the C++ substring position is invalid.
5. Add focused unit tests in the library module for observed regular, irregular, case-sensitive, separator, acronym, Unicode, and boundary behavior.
6. Build with `cargo build --release` in `/output`, producing `/output/target/release/test15`.
7. Compare the Rust binary byte-for-byte against `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable` for:
   - the five supplied examples (`cat`, `dog`, `person`, `child`, `mouse`)
   - no arguments
   - multiple arguments and more than five arguments
   - underscore/camelCase/acronym/Unicode inputs
   - uncountables and `isPlural` edge cases
   - `demodulize` namespace inputs
8. If all comparisons match, report the build artifact and verification results.
